prompt_en: Photographic study of visible garment fit, showing a woman in a concrete clothing-fit situation. Use the attached image as visual guidance for her face and dark bob with wispy bangs. The photograph catches her in a harbor maintenance alcove at midday during a rain break, beside a waist-high wooden workbench and the open field repair kit she is about to carry back to the boat. Rain beads remain on the aluminum case lid; a coiled mooring line and the bright opening onto wet harbor paving explain why this small pause matters. Her concentration on the last equipment check softens into a warm, slightly amused glance toward the photographer, while her body stays engaged with the task. She wears a smooth charcoal cotton-jersey T-shirt under an olive utility vest, and a thin crinkled blue nylon rain jacket as the outer layer. The T-shirt lies close along her upper torso with modest stretch over the ribs. The vest has firmer woven front and back panels with a narrow visible gap on the camera-near right side. Two separate black webbing bridges cross this side gap, one just below the ribs and one at the waist. At each olive vest side connection, one webbing section is box-stitched to its front fabric anchor and another to its rear fabric anchor; these two sections join through a central rectangular metal buckle on that same vest. Both green fabric anchor patches, the two webbing paths and the buckle stay visibly distinct across the gap. The lower buckle is just above her right hip; the upper buckle is below her right ribs. The vest front zipper is closed from the lower edge to the sternum, leaving the upper V opening to reveal the T-shirt. The blue nylon rain jacket is oversized as one coherent outer garment: its dropped shoulder seams sit outside her shoulder joints, its wide sleeves match the broad hanging torso, and a visible air margin separates this same jacket from the firmer vest beneath. The open near-side jacket panel folds back behind her right upper arm, exposing both vest side connections; the blue panel then hangs behind the hip. Its roomy right sleeve forms soft crinkles around her bent elbow, while the cuff is fastened at the wrist. The three layers have distinct edges and distinct degrees of ease. She stands with both feet planted on the level floor, hips a little back from the workbench. Her far-side left palm rests beside the open kit, supporting a slight forward lean. Her near-side right thumb and index finger pinch the loose webbing tail below the lower vest buckle, pulling the tail gently downward after it exits that fastening. Her right hand stays below the buckle line, leaving the metal fastening and both green fabric anchor patches visible. Her right elbow points gently outward, preserving a clear view of the garment side. Frame from the top of her head to mid-thigh. The camera looks from her right-front three-quarter direction at chest height, giving lateral room to the vest gap and the repair kit. A soft overcast skylight illuminates her face, layered fabric and functional hardware evenly; wet paving supplies a quieter bright background. Natural perspective, moderate depth of field, visible skin texture, restrained documentary fashion photography. Let the inviting glance carry a subtle personal appeal while the garment relationships and the pause before departure remain the center of the image.
